messages:
charlie: Heads-up — I'm seeing p99 tail spikes after the kernel-selector change (deployed ~0900). Short requests (<=32 tokens) that should be cheap are occasionally getting huge latencies. I traced a couple to batch admission ignoring KV cache footprint estimates, so the batch assembler packs a bunch of requests and then we hit soft OOM pressure and start evicting KV pages mid-batch.

priya: ack. can you paste the trace and the kv metrics you saw? alg or exact repro would help. :eyes:

charlie: quick snippet from the tracer + metrics:
```
model=model-x, gpu=0
batch_size=18 -> p50 12ms, p99 420ms (expected p99 ~60ms)
kv_estimates per request: [1.2GB, 40MB, 60MB, 1.1GB, ...]
free_kv_before_batch=2.1GB
free_kv_mid_batch=120MB -> oom-guard evict ~200MB -> per-evict pause 25-45ms
stack: batch-assembler -> continuous-batcher -> runtime-kernel-selector
```
The pattern: a couple large-kv requests slip into the same batch with many small ones. When eviction happens we see cascaded token latency.

dan: interesting — the kernel-selector change favored the faster fp16 kernels for short sequences which reduced per-token CPU overhead, but it also relaxed admission gating (we removed a conservative kv-check because it regressed throughput in microbench). Looks like throughput win but made us vulnerable to KV pressure.

len: proposal: introduce an "OOM gate" in admission that combines a fast kv-footprint estimator + slotting prioritization. Key ideas:
- estimate_kv(request) cheap estimator (first-token analysis / model metadata)
- batch_slots = ceil(token_budget / slot_weight)
- each request consumes slots = max(1, ceil(estimated_kv / KV_SLOT_BYTES))
- if sum(slots) + reserved_slots > available_slots => either stall or demote requests (low-prio)
- fallback: if demotion still over budget, build a mini-batch with only low-kv requests and route large-kv ones to a low-concurrency "wide" pool

priya: +1. A few extra notes: we should keep the estimator super cheap (no tensor ops), avoid false positives (overestimating drops throughput), and tune KV_SLOT_BYTES per GPU type. Also we can combine with kernel selection by mapping large-kv requests to kernels that are more memory-friendly even if slightly slower.

charlie: here's a quick admission pseudo we can try in the assembler: 
```
// run in assembler main loop
kv_free = metrics.kv_free_estimate()
reserved = kv_reserve_soft  // e.g. 512MB
available = max(0, kv_free - reserved)
slots_available = floor(available / KV_SLOT_BYTES)
batch_slots = 0
for req in queue.peek(N):
  req_slots = max(1, ceil(est_kv(req) / KV_SLOT_BYTES))
  if batch_slots + req_slots <= slots_available:
    batch.add(req); batch_slots += req_slots
  else:
    if req.priority == HIGH:
      // try to push lower-prio ones out
      continue
    else:
      demote(req) // mark for later pool
```
This is intentionally conservative. We can start with KV_SLOT_BYTES=256MB and reserved=512MB and iterate.

dan: profiling notes from local runs with this logic: p99 drops from ~420ms -> ~90ms for the repro. Throughput slightly down on synthetic mix (2-3%) but much better tail. Kernel change interaction: when we force large-kv -> memory-friendly kernel, kernel selection latency rises +2ms per token but we avoid eviction stalls.

len: rollout plan suggestion:
1) feature-flagged change in assembler + quick sim harness (existing loadgen)
2) collect metrics: p50/p95/p99, kv-evict-count, eviction-latency, throughput
3) A/B: traffic split 10/90 for 1 hour, watch p99 SLOs
4) if regressions visible revert via rollout flag

priya: also add logs for decision reason-code (REJECT_KV_GUARD, DEMOTED_SLOT, KERNEL_FALLBACK) so we can query later. we should avoid noisy logs (sample first 1000 decisions).

charlie: I'll write the patch and bench harness tonight. ping me if you want to co-author. plan: land behind flag, run sim across model-x & model-y, tune KV_SLOT_BYTES per GPU.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/assembler#452 by charlie -> staging. Triggered tests: perf-smoke, kv-prober-smoke. ETA ~5m. :shipit:

len: one more note — we should add a lightweight kernel-selection cost model that accounts for eviction risk. right now selector just compares latency curves; add a memory-pressure term so it prefers a slightly slower but lower-kv path under pressure. That will reduce oscillation between throughput vs tail.

charlie: agreed. i'll add a small hook so selector asks current_kv_pressure() before choosing. that should keep admission and kernel selection aligned.

priya: awesome. once we have logs we can build an alert for eviction-spike -> auto-rollback if p99 > threshold for 5m.

dan: tl;dr: add conservative slotting + OOM gate, map large-kv to mem-friendly kernels, flagged rollout, observe p99 improvements in local sim.

charlie: thanks team — starting the PR now.
